Question: Q15. Your bookstore uploads a new catalog CSV every month. If the new file has a column added in the middle of the exist
Student Answer:
CSV file has no embedded schema. When Athena queries a CSV table, it maps values to columns by position, based on the schema registered in the Glue Data Catalog. If we insert a new column in the middle, every column after it shifts one position to the right. But the Glue catalog still expects the old order, so Athena maps the wrong values to the wrong columns. No error is thrown, but the data just comes back wrong. 

However, it doesn't the problem in Parquet. Parquet is self-describing, so every Parquet files embeds its own schema, including column names and types. Athena reads the column metadata from the file itself and matches values by column names, not by position. So, if a new column apperas in the middle, Athena simply reads each column by name, places the new column where it belongs. There will be no misalignment, no silent corruption.
Correct Answer: CSV maps columns positionally â€” Athena reads the 1st value as column 1, 2nd as column 2, etc. A column inserted in the middle shifts every subsequent column, mapping wrong data to wrong columns (prices in rating column, etc.) with no error message. Parquet stores column names inside the file and maps by name, not position, so reordering/adding columns doesn't cause misalignment. Parquet is inherently safer for schema evolution.
